$~$

The overall purpose of this project is to identify putative associations between genes involved in tissue development and p53. As germline p53 mutations would be present in all cells from conception, they would be carried through all developmental tissues and their organ derivatives, and thus could shape the unique epigenetics specific to tissues. Thus, if there are many developmental genes with putative associations with p53, they could be dysregulated by germline p53 mutations and lead to predilections for cancer. Moreover, it would also be interesting to see if p53 has more putative associations with developmental genes in tissues with germline cancers vs. in tissues with somatic cancers, in which somatic mutations arise after development. Also, we want to identify the number of p53 binding sites across normal tissues subjected to ATAC-seq to understand its binding footprints in different organs.

$~$

# **Input Data** {#inputdata}

$~$

To begin our studies of whether p53 regulates developmental genes, we first need to understand which genes are expressed and important for human germ layer and organ development. Thankfully, over the years, there have been multiple transcriptomic studies in human embryos on gastrulation, where the 3 germ layers arise about 2-3 weeks into embryonic development, and organogenesis, where most organ development occurs about 4-8 weeks into embryonic development. Key studies have ranged from assessing differentially-expressed genes (DEGs) over time in the whole embryo [@fang2010; @yi2010] to transcriptomics and epigenomics in individual embryonic organs [@gerrard2016; @gerrard2020] to single-cell transcriptomics of gastrulating and early organogenic embryos [@tyser2021; @xu2023].

$~$

Importantly, all these studies have easily-accessible lists of genes that can be analysed further, which is why I draw on supplementary information from all these papers to identify vital genes both for specific organs as well as temporal differences during embryonic development. I also evaluate if the genes identified are possible p53 targets through a database (<http://www.targetgenereg.org/>) [@fischer2022] and via overlap with previously-reported studies of known p53 targets [@fischer2017; @nguyen2018]. 23 Carnegie Stages (CS) [@orahilly1987; @orahilly2010] are employed to characterise where embryos are temporally during development as they describe when features arise during the embryonic period. CS6-7 is when gastrulation occurs [@tan2014] and CS9-23 is when organogenesis occurs [@geng2010], which is why it is critical for any developmental genes identified to be expressed during these stages.

$~$

Supplementary File 1 from @gerrard2016 contains the embryonic samples used in the study (all within CS14-22), tissue-specific genes contributing to "metagenes", and extreme genes from lineage-guided PCA (LgPCA) to identify tissue-specific signatures, among other types of data.

Supplementary File 2 from @gerrard2016 contains all the gene annotations used in their RNA-seq.

$~$

Supplementary Files 1, 4, and 5 from @gerrard2020 contain the embryonic samples used in the study (all within CS14-22), promoter methylation states of nearly 20,000 genes across all tissues tested, and gene sets of genes expressed in 1 tissue vs repressed in other tissues, respectively.

$~$

Supplementary File 1 from @xu2023 contains the cell types and DEGs (which also feature most canonical markers of cell types reported in the literature) identified in single-cell transcriptomics of CS12-16 human embryos, with abbreviations denoted as below:

-   IM = intermediate mesoderm
-   LPM = lateral plate mesoderm
-   PGC = primordial germ cell

$~$

Supplementary Table S2 from @fang2010 contains 2148 genes identified after a self-organizing map with singular value decomposition (SOM-SVD) analysis of 5441 DEGs in CS9--14 human embryos and subjected to clustering that identified temporal differences in expression across embryological development. Genes in clusters 1-3 were associated with organogenesis initiation, while genes in clusters 5 and 6 were associated with organogenesis establishment, and are thus called early organ and late organs genes, respectively, later on in this code.

$~$

Supplementary Table 3 from @yi2010 contains genes identified after a SOM analysis of 5358 DEGs in CS10--23 human embryos and analysed in 3 expression groups that identified temporal differences in expression across embryological development. Genes in the "up" group temporally increase in expression across the samples, genes in the "arch" group have peak expression during weeks 5-7, and genes in the "down" group temporally decrease in expression across the samples.

$~$

Supplementary Table 1 from @tyser2021 contains marker genes of cell types identified in single-cell transcriptomics of a CS7 human gastrula, with abbreviations denoted as below:

-   Epiblast (Epi)
-   Ectoderm (amniotic/embryonic) (EAE)
-   Primitive streak (PS)
-   Nascent mesoderm (NM)
-   Emergent mesoderm (EM)
-   Advanced mesoderm (AM)
-   Extraembryonic mesoderm (ExM)
-   Axial mesoderm (AxM)
-   Endoderm (Endo)
-   Haemato-endothelial progenitors (HEP)
-   Erythroblasts (Ery)

$~$

I will also include organ-specific studies in human embryos for selected core tissues in Li-Fraumeni Syndrome and tissues that frequently have somatic TP53 mutations.

Supplemental Data 2 from @delvalle2023 contains DEGs in 7 wpc - 11.5 wpc human adrenal cortices, while Supplemental Data 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4 from @delvalle2023 contains marker genes from single-cell analysis in 6wpc, 6wpc+6d, and 8wpc+5d human adrenal cortices.

$~$

Supplementary Dataset 2 from @delvalle2017 contains DEGs in CS17-CS23 and F1-3 (fetal) human adrenal glands.

$~$

Supplementary Tables S1 to S5 from @zeng2023 contain DEGs from CS3-CS12 human embryos, heads, and brains.

$~$

Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 from @cao2023 contain DEGs in lung development from CS12-21 human embryos.

$~$

Supplementary Table S2 from @feng2014 contains genes that temporally changed in expression across human embryo lung development. Figure 3 from @feng2014 depicts the 27 temporal changes that each gene is assigned to, so I will select genes that have the highest expression in the 3-5wpc whole embryo (WholeE) and 6-8wpc early lung (EarlyL).

$~$

Supplementary Table S1 from @he2021 contains DEGs in human embryo limb buds 5wpc and long bone 8wpc development.

$~$

Supplementary Tables 3, 5, and 9 from @cebola2015 contain lists of genes implicated in CS16-CS18 human embryo pancreas development.

$~$

Table 2 from @jennings2015 contains genes that affect human pancreas development.

$~$

Supplementary Table S3 from @fischer2017 contains a census of 343 high-confidence p53 target genes which will be used to see how many putative p53-regulated developmental genes overlap with known targets.

$~$

Supplementary Table ST8 from @nguyen2018 contains a p53 target cistrome of 943 genes which will also be used to see how many putative p53-regulated developmental genes overlap with known targets.

$~$

Table 1 and Supplementary Table S2 from @wang2020a contain lists of p73 targets validated in human cancer cell lines.

Datasets S1A, S1B, and S1C from @rosenbluth2011 contain lists of genes commonly regulated by p73, p63, and p53.

Table 1 from @fontemaggi2002 contains lists of genes regulated by p53 and p73 in a human cancer line.

Table 1 from @vikhanskaya2001 contains lists of genes upregulated or downregulated by p73 in another human cancer line.

As comprehensive p73 cistrome/census lists are not rigorously reported in the literature, and a rare database of p73 direct targets [@sbisa2007] is now defunct and inaccessible, these lists only provide some indication of the targets that p73 regulates.

$~$

Supplementary Table S1 from @singh2019 contains differentially-expressed genes after H1299 cells transduced with p53 mutant P152L, a residue of interest in adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), were injected into mice and tumors underwent RNA sequencing. This list, when crossed with p53-regulated developmental genes, can identify genes specifically changed following mutant p53 activity.

$~$

I also downloaded DEGs from GEO2R analyses (<https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/geo2r/?acc=GSE131592>) of isogenic mutant human AML cells from @boettcher2019 that underwent bulk RNA sequencing. Briefly, in the paper's data availability section I clicked on the link to the RNAseq data filed in GEO under GSE131592 (<https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE131592>). Here I downloaded the entire TAR file of raw counts data for all 96 samples (<https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/download/?acc=GSE131592&format=file>) which I then unzipped into a folder on the computer. I also clicked on "Analyze with GEO2R" to do the differential gene expression analysis online. I manually created every contrast for all replicates per sample (i.e. mutant vs WT or mutant vs KO for DMSO, daunorubicin, K562, and MOLM13 cells) where the mutant was defined first and the control (WT or KO) was defined second for the fold change. In the Options tab I then set p-value adjustment to Benjamini and Hochberg (FDR), significance cutoff to 0.05, and log2FC threshold to 1, checked the box to show the volcano and mean-difference plots, and clicked analyze. After the analysis ran, I downloaded the entire table of genes with all possible columns as TSV files which I have read in here. I also downloaded the R scripts for each contrast's analysis which are saved on the computer as TXT files.

$~$

For many of these GEO2R studies, Duncan Parkes at the LICR was able to extract raw gene counts, which I have then read into R below.

$~$

As we are also interested in a link between LFS, senescence, and macrophages to tie these analyses together with the work I did at the NIH, I wanted to see if genes upregulated in the LFS studies above were also implicated in senescence or the M2 macrophage phenotype. Thus, I have drawn on the macrophage studies from above and on the studies below which are databases of genes implicated in human senescence and reviews indicating genes implicated in macrophage polarization.

$~$

I downloaded all human cell senescence genes from the Cell Senescence Gene Database at <https://csgene.bioinfo-minzhao.org/download.cgi> which was created from @zhao2016. The paper compiled hundreds of human genes that have been described in multiple databases and published studies as involved in different pathways in cellular senescence, which was then posted to the database with additional information.

Briefly, I went to <https://csgene.bioinfo-minzhao.org/download.cgi> and clicked on the flat file for human cell senescence genes which opened in a webpage. I then highlighted everything and saved it as a TXT file which I have then read in here.

$~$

I also downloaded genes associated with cell senescence and a gene expression signature of senescence from the CellAge Database Build 3 at <https://genomics.senescence.info/cells/index.html> which was created from @avelar2020 for CellAge and @chatsirisupachai2019 for CellSignature. The CellAge paper compiled hundreds of genes from studies that manipulated gene expression in human cells that caused them to undergo or inhibit senescence. The CellSignature paper established a gene signature of replicative senescence after a meta-analysis of many human microarray datasets. These databases are part of a larger umbrella of databases called Human Ageing Genomic Resources (HAGR) which is discussed in @tacutu2017. Other aging databases in this umbrella include a GenAge database of ageing-related genes, an AnAge database of animal ageing and longevity, a GenDR database of genes involved with life-extending effects after diet restriction, a LongevityMap database of human gene association studies of longevity, and a DrugAge database with ageing or longevity-associated compounds.

Briefly, I went to <https://genomics.senescence.info/cells/index.html> and scrolled down to the Downloading CellAge section. I clicked on the CSV file to download all genes associated with cell senescence and the CSV file to download the gene expression signature, which both downloaded to the computer as zipped files. I then unzipped them which yielded a TSV and CSV file, respectively, and have read in both of these files here. Both unzipped folders also have respective release HTML files associated with each TSV or CSV file which indicates the database build version. The CellAge data indicates Build 3 but the CellSignature was unchanged from Build 2 in Build 3 so it indicates Build 2 in the downloaded file.

$~$

I also have read in here as a vector M1 and M2 macrophage phenotype inducing genes depicted in Figure 1 of @chen2023, Figure 1 of @wang2014, and Figure 2 of @ni2016a. Importantly, I have only included genes triggered after stimuli I used in the NIH to induce macrophages, i.e. LPS, IFN-gamma, and IL-4. 

$~$

I have also used the UCSC Xena platform (<https://xenabrowser.net/>) [@goldman2020] and TCGA TARGET GTEx study [@vivian2017] therein (where TCGA adult tumor, TARGET pediatric tumor, and GTEx normal tissue samples were re-analyzed by the same RNA-seq pipeline that re-aligned the reads to hg38 and called gene expression using RSEM and Kallisto) to perform genome-wide differential gene expression analysis in tumors vs normal tissues for adrenal, brain, lung, liver, kidney, and pancreas. These tissues were chosen as they are core Li-Fraumeni syndrome tissues or tissues which have cancers with somatic p53 mutations and I have developmental genesets for each in my embryological study compilation.

This pipeline only allows a maximum of 2,000 samples to run through it, which all these individual organ analyses met. This analysis gives a general overview of DEGs in these cancers but doesn't exactly answer our question of which p53 developmental target genes are downregulated in cancers with specific p53 mutations. However, I couldn't do this analysis for limb and soft tissue tumors as the tissue of origin of [sarcoma tumors in TCGA](https://www.cancer.gov/ccg/research/genome-sequencing/tcga/studied-cancers/sarcoma-study) was unclear, so I couldn't specifically choose GTEx normal tissues to compare with.

For this analysis, I first went to the [How do I compare tumor vs normal expression?](https://ucsc-xena.gitbook.io/project/how-do-i/tumor-vs-normal) help page, clicked on the [TCGA TARGET GTEx study](https://xenabrowser.net/?bookmark=057c5fe67d5d79488b843d7a6e1a9840) indicated there, in the new page that opened clicked on Differential expression from the main category E top right corner dropdown, and in the new page that opened I selected group 1 as all TCGA tumors for the tissue of interest, selected group 2 as the GTEx normal tissue of interest, did not change any other parameters on the page, and clicked submit. Thus, I only assigned the groups for differential expression and directly clicked submit without changing anything in the PCA/t-SNE or DGE analysis sections. These differential expression steps are also in the video on the [Differential Gene Expression](https://ucsc-xena.gitbook.io/project/overview-of-features/differential-gene-expression) help page.

Xena generated stable weblinks of the full pipelines with viewable code which I have pasted below. From these links I downloaded the DEG csv files which I have read in here, and I have also downloaded the code notebooks for each analysis.

-   Adrenal: <http://analysis.xenahubs.net/a41c3758732fdb8dec454830af72b089723fc27f/>
-   Brain: <http://analysis.xenahubs.net/0497b6b25a40d039226febd3e76e2954ae2f92cb/>
-   Lung: <http://analysis.xenahubs.net/650397090977375df466c6888d6d6e288f0ba63b/>
-   Liver: <http://analysis.xenahubs.net/edaddd6940770e88c3973d442c4283e843eb3849/>
-   Kidney: <http://analysis.xenahubs.net/abac98ecab855fdd698472d801d29c2f594500bd/>
-   Pancreas: <http://analysis.xenahubs.net/1fcd1a2b36980126557bb7686ac15acc40332557/>

$~$

I have also used the ICGC Data Portal (<https://dcc.icgc.org/>) [] and 12 studies therein (below) to procure open simple somatic mutations and exp_seq files. Since there are not many isogenic p53 mutant gene expression studies in the literature, we will try to use gene expression information from patients with cancer and with or without p53 mutations of interest to see if p53-regulated genes in development are differentially expressed after specific mutations in p53. This approach will have many confounders, such as other mutant genes in tumors, but we will try to match mutational profiles of these other genes between the groups created and only analyse within studies.

For this analysis, I did an advanced search in the ICGC Data Portal for patients with mutant TP53, available EXP-S (sequencing expression) data, and cancers in my tissues of interest i.e. lung, pancreas, brain, liver, kidney, and bone (they did not have adrenal tumor information). There were over 1300 individuals from 16 projects that matched this criteria, from which I then opened up every distinct study to check if the projects were pertinent. The BOCA-FR study was not used because it examined patients with Ewing sarcoma rather than osteosarcoma which is the tumor I needed. The LIRI-JP and LICA-FR studies were not used since they included patients with virus-associated hepatocellular carcinoma or patients with hepatocellular carcinoma secondary to alcohol and adiposity, respectively. The PAEN-AU study was not used since it included patients with endocrine neoplasms rather than pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma which is the predominant tumor type I wanted. I've copied here the exact search link I used to get the 1300+ patients and 16 studies (<https://dcc.icgc.org/search?filters=%7B%22gene%22:%7B%22id%22:%7B%22is%22:%5B%22ENSG00000141510%22%5D%7D%7D,%22donor%22:%7B%22availableDataTypes%22:%7B%22is%22:%5B%22exp_seq%22%5D%7D,%22primarySite%22:%7B%22is%22:%5B%22Lung%22,%22Pancreas%22,%22Brain%22,%22Liver%22,%22Kidney%22,%22Bone%22%5D%7D%7D%7D&donors=%7B%22from%22:1301,%22sort%22:%22primarySite%22,%22order%22:%22asc%22,%22size%22:50%7D>).

Of the 12 studies that remained, I clicked on "Open in DCC Data Releases" and downloaded the simple_somatic_mutation.open and exp_seq tsv.gz files (below are the direct links to DCC Data Releases), which I then unzipped and read into this code as TSVs. As I don't have adrenal or bone tumor information from ICGC, there aren't enough core LFS tissues to juxtapose with the other LFS tissues.

-   GBM-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/GBM-US>
-   LGG-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/LGG-US>
-   PBCA-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/PBCA-US> This study was not actually used because its somatic mutation file didn't load mutant allele counts so the mutant allele fraction could not be calculated.
-   KIRC-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/KIRC-US>
-   RECA-EU: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/RECA-EU>
-   KIRP-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/KIRP-US>
-   LIHC-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/LIHC-US>
-   LUSC-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/LUSC-US>
-   LUAD-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/LUAD-US>
-   PACA-AU: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/PACA-AU>
-   PACA-CA: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/PACA-CA>
-   PAAD-US: <https://dcc.icgc.org/releases/current/Projects/PAAD-US>

$~$

We are interested in whether mutations affecting splicing in TP53 (picked up from germline p53 analyses) indeed lead to changed expression of p53 isoforms, including our senescence-reversing isoform of interest Δ133p53α. The ideal datasets to evaluate this would be isogenic WT and p53-splice-mutant cells which underwent long-read bulk RNA sequencing. However, due to the absence of such datasets in the literature, proxies have been utilized, namely TCGA p53-splice mutant and other mutant cases. Although there will be many confounders here, most notably highly variable background mutations in other genes, demographics will be matched as closely as possible programatically.

To address this, TCGA splice mutant (only T125T is mutated in cases) vs other mutant (cases have another mutation only once) cases (clinical details and gene expression/mutation files) were downloaded from the legacy version (v1) of the Genomic Data Commons (GDC) <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/v1/> []. M133T and M133R were other splicing mutations of interest but only handful of patients with cancer in TCGA had these mutations. Consequently, they could not be included for analyses as at least 2 individuals would be needed for each condition. Cases were selected after extensive filtering with many requirements, including using studies which had at least 2 patients each with splicing or other mutations, each case having only one mutation in p53, each case having only 1 associated gene expression and mutation file, and broad matches on sex and tumor stage across entire datasets. First splicing mutant cases were queried and then other mutant cases were identified, each saved into their own case sets on GDC.

In this manner, 19 splicing mutant and 226 other mutant cases were selected and their associated open access gene expression and mutation files (RNAseq augmented STAR gene counts and ensemble masked somatic mutations) were added from the associated GDC repository section to the GDC cart. Gene expression files were checked to ensure only primary tumour files were added to the cart and not files of matched normal tissues. There were exactly 2n total files for n cases, and the cart along with associated files (biospecimen, clinical, sample sheet, metadata, case sets, etc.) were subsequently downloaded and unzipped in folders on the computer. Below are the cases which were used:

-   Splicing mutant cases: <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/v1/exploration?filters=%7B%22op%22%3A%22and%22%2C%22content%22%3A%5B%7B%22op%22%3A%22in%22%2C%22content%22%3A%7B%22field%22%3A%22cases.case_id%22%2C%22value%22%3A%5B%22set_id%3A8b08b6865d79a21ca098e6d28b65f995aab963aa9c00938837e8e7f0960ef2ea199886772b0c14b32d594cdbafce69f650f396f299a7a277e740b670c670c03e%22%5D%7D%7D%5D%7D&searchTableTab=cases>
-   Other mutant cases: <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/v1/exploration?filters=%7B%22op%22%3A%22and%22%2C%22content%22%3A%5B%7B%22op%22%3A%22in%22%2C%22content%22%3A%7B%22field%22%3A%22cases.case_id%22%2C%22value%22%3A%5B%22set_id%3A36f4adf458c681bf96fbc0fb129bc4002d6c8f7247bff38615503c25fc2fb8108b1063b63ed725c4c42093a93e2a3b28563761f0793160409b79892a54bcf22f%22%5D%7D%7D%5D%7D&searchTableTab=cases>

$~$

The adrenal gland is a key tissue of interest, given ACC's high diagonsis rate in Li-Fraumeni Syndrome and the organ's origin from two germ layers. Thus, we wanted to see if p53 developmental target genes implicated in the embryonic adrenal gland are also dysregulated after p53 mutations in ACC cells.

The ideal dataset for doing this would be RNAseq from germline-mutant ACC, but due to its absence, I procured TCGA-ACC cases from the GDC that either had mutations in p53 or didn't have p53 mutations. Cases with CNV changes in p53 were removed in both cohorts, but due to the inherently small n numbers based on mutation presence or absence, there wasn't much further filtering of cases on other criteria, so each p53 mutation in the mutant cohort is only present in 1 case, for example. 

In this manner, 10 mutant and 40 wild-type ACC cancer cases were selected and their associated open access gene expression and mutation files (RNAseq augmented STAR gene counts and ensemble masked somatic mutations) were added from the associated GDC repository section to the GDC cart. Gene expression files were checked to ensure only primary tumour files were added to the cart and not files of matched normal tissues. There were exactly 2n total files for n cases, and the cart along with associated files (biospecimen, clinical, sample sheet, metadata, case sets, etc.) were subsequently downloaded and unzipped in folders on the computer. Below are the cases which were used:

-   p53 mutant cases: <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/v1/exploration?filters=%7B%22content%22%3A%5B%7B%22content%22%3A%7B%22field%22%3A%22cases.case_id%22%2C%22value%22%3A%5B%22set_id%3AEPTArQvo7ct_m_2D6M-tWQ%22%5D%7D%2C%22op%22%3A%22IN%22%7D%5D%2C%22op%22%3A%22AND%22%7D>
-   p53 wild type cases: <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/v1/exploration?filters=%7B%22content%22%3A%5B%7B%22content%22%3A%7B%22field%22%3A%22cases.case_id%22%2C%22value%22%3A%5B%22set_id%3AKkVnoLhawOsku43H0IIXMQ%22%5D%7D%2C%22op%22%3A%22IN%22%7D%5D%2C%22op%22%3A%22AND%22%7D>

$~$

In addition to this embryological genes pursuit, we are also interested in whether ATAC-seq studies of different normal human cell lines and normal human tissues can reveal how many p53 binding sites are open and present across tissues, as differences in chromatin accessibility can also explain why targets are differentially transcribed. Thus, we are examining normal tissues collected in an ATAC-seq database (<https://bio.liclab.net/ATACdb/index.php>) [@wang2020] for the p53 footprint, i.e. number of binding sites, in normal tissues.

$~$

The ATACdb database utilized is at <https://bio.liclab.net/ATACdb/index.php> [@wang2020].

All TFs' footprints for all samples on ATACdb were downloaded from <https://bio.liclab.net/ATACdb/Download.php> (Download accessible chromatin region,TF footprint and associated gene \--\> TF footprint \--\> download .txt file).

All ATACdb sample metadata was downloaded from <https://bio.liclab.net/ATACdb/Data_Browse.php> with no parameters selected (white rectangle at above left area of Showing 1 to 20 of 1,493 entries is clickable if you hover over it, so click on that and a csv file is downloaded of all sample information).

All the data across all samples and TFs have been downloaded for now, but they will be subsetted to just p53 information in normal tissues in this code.

$~$

As another pursuit, I also want to see if macrophage polarization genes are controlled by p53, meaning that d133p53a could modulate p53 regulation and induce the M1 phenotype. Thus, I'm compiling genes from the literature that are known to promote the M1 or M2 phenotype. In particular, Figure 1 from @chen2023, Figure 1 from @wang2014, and Figure 2 from @ni2016a all contain lists of genes that favor each phenotype. I am only selecting genes induced from IL-4/13, IFN-gamma, LPS, and GM-CSF in these figures as these are the stimuli I used when differentiating my macrophages at the NIH.

$~$

In this code, I have then read in all the files I want to use for my analysis. I have added parameters and functions to trim unneeded rows or columns as I have seen the files beforehand.

$~$

```{r inputdata, results = 'hide', message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
                         tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$file_id,
                         "/",
                         tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$file_name))) %>% 
  unlist()


# see whether file paths are valid, and subset list to only true file paths
bloop <- bloop[which((lapply(1:length(bloop), 
               function(x) file.exists(bloop[[x]]))) == "TRUE")]


# read in all files from filepaths, add temporary names to list elements e.g. folders for gene counts tables
bloop_select <- bloop[which(lapply(1:length(bloop),
             FUN = function(x) grepl(bloop[[x]],
                                     pattern = "\\.tsv$")) == TRUE)] # only gene counts files

tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list <- lapply(1:length(bloop_select), 
                                    FUN = function(x) (read.delim(file = bloop_select[[x]],
                                                                  header = TRUE,
                                                                  sep = "\t",
                                                                  skip = 1,
                                                                  na.strings = c("", 
                                                                                 "NA")) %>% 
                                                         drop_na(gene_name)))

names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list) <- str_extract(bloop_select, 
                                                "cart.*\\.tsv$") %>%
  gsub("cart/|/.*\\.tsv$",
       "", 
       .) %>% 
  unique()


# replace temporary file names with matched case id, case or control 
names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list) <- ifelse(names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list) %in% tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$file_id, 
                                           paste0(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$case_id[match(names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list),
                                                                             tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$file_id)],
                                                  "_",
                                                  tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$case_ctrl[match(names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list),
                                                                             tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_rnaseqpaths_df$file_id)]), 
                                           "notyet") %>% 
  unique()


# add sample/case names to counts cols specific to each df, not gene cols
tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_list <- lapply(1:length(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list),
                                             FUN = function(x) {
                                               i <- tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list[[x]]
                                               names(i)[4:ncol(i)] <- paste0(names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list)[[x]],
                                                                             "_",
                                                                             names(i)[4:ncol(i)])
                                               i  
                                             })


# remove hyphens because invalid for rownames which samples will eventually be for metadata
names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_list) <- names(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_gene_counts_list) %>% 
  gsub("\\-",
       "_",
       .)


# combine all counts tables into 1 mega df and remove processed tpm and fpkm columns, stranded columns since unstranded should be used, and again remove hyphens so that samples can be used for metadata rows
tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_df <- Reduce(full_join,
                                           tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_list) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-contains(c("tpm",
                            "fpkm",
                            "_first",
                            "_second"))) %>% 
  distinct()

colnames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_df) <- gsub("\\-",
                                                   "_",
                                                   colnames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_df))


# make gene and sample metadata by pulling out annotation columns from previous dfs, adding hgnc annotations to gene metadata, adding contrasts for deseq definitions of test and ctrls, removing hyphens to allow rowname assignment, moving items to match on to rows 
tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_genes_metadata <- tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_df %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(gene_id,
                  gene_name,
                  gene_type)) %>% 
  mutate(ensembl_gene_id = gsub("\\..*",
                        "",
                        gene_id)) %>% 
  left_join(.,
            hgnc %>% 
              dplyr::select(c(symbol,
                              ensembl_gene_id,
                              entrez_id,
                              locus_group,
                              name)),
            by = "ensembl_gene_id",
            multiple = "first") %>% # just first match as 1 LINC has 2 names
  dplyr::select(-c(gene_name,
                   gene_type)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene_id") 


tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata <- tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_sheet %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(case_id,
                  sample_id,
                  case_ctrl)) %>% 
  mutate(matching_case_id = paste0(case_id,
                                   "_",
                                   case_ctrl)) %>% 
  mutate(contrast = paste0(case_ctrl)) %>% 
  distinct()

# add more information from clinical parameters to sample metadata
tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata <- left_join(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata, 
                                                 tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_clinical %>% 
                                                   dplyr::select(c(case_submitter_id,
                                                                   age_at_index,
                                                                   ethnicity,
                                                                   gender, 
                                                                   race, 
                                                                   vital_status, 
                                                                   ajcc_clinical_m, 
                                                                   ajcc_pathologic_n, 
                                                                   ajcc_pathologic_stage,
                                                                   ajcc_pathologic_t, 
                                                                   classification_of_tumor,
                                                                   icd_10_code, 
                                                                   morphology, 
                                                                   primary_diagnosis,
                                                                   site_of_resection_or_biopsy, 
                                                                   tissue_or_organ_of_origin, 
                                                                   tumor_grade)), 
                                                 by = c("case_id" = "case_submitter_id")) %>% 
  arrange(case_ctrl) %>%
  distinct() 


tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata$matching_case_id <- gsub("\\-",
                                              "_",
                                              tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata$matching_case_id)

tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata <- tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata %>% 
  column_to_rownames("matching_case_id") %>%
  distinct()


# make final counts table df for deseq
tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named <- tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named_df %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(gene_name,
                   gene_type)) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("gene_id")

colnames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named) <- gsub("_unstranded$",
                                                           "",
                                                           colnames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named))

# need to ensure mega df of counts has colnames in same order as rows of sample annotation table
tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named <- tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named[,rownames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata)]
identical(rownames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_sample_metadata),
          colnames(tcga_acc_p53mutvswt_counts_samples_named)) # should be TRUE if rownames and colnames are same
```

# **Cleaning Input Data** {#cleaningdata}

$~$

Next, I cleaned the data into appropriate dataframe formats to use downstream in analysis, with details per the below code.

$~$

```{r datacleaning, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = 'hide'}
# transpose genesets so that tissues are columns and genes are rows after making tissues the initial df rownames, removing number of gene columns, and removing rownames (random placeholder colnames in orig df) after transposing
cleaned_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020 <- orig_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020 %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Tissue") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-`Number of genes`) %>%
  t() %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# replace misformatted excel values with gene names (erroneously rewritten as dates in excel and converted to random numbers in R) and 
cleaned_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020["Brain"][cleaned_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020["Brain"] == "36951"] <- "MARCHF1"
cleaned_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020["Heart..LV"][cleaned_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020["Heart..LV"] == "40603"] <- "MARCHF11"

# update gene names per hgnc and genecards.org
# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_genesets_expvsrep_gerrard_2020 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1) %>%
  mutate(Genes = gsub("ORF",
                      "orf",
                      Genes))

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 76

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# need to clean metagenes df so that we have columns of metagenes and rows of genes
# first, remove Genes: prefix in comma'd list of genes, add all data to rownames and then remove genes from row names by duplicating NMF metagene info there and adding _keep suffix to rows we want to retain i.e. rows of genes
cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016 <- orig_metagene_gerrard_2016 %>% 
  data.frame()

cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$...1 <- gsub("Genes:  ", 
                                            "",
                                            cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$...1)

row.names(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016) <- cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$...1

row.names(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016)[seq(2, nrow(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016), 2)] <- paste0(row.names(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016)[seq(1, nrow(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016), 2)],
                                                                                                     "_keep") 

# then remove any rows which mention NMF metagene so that only genes lists are left, make metagenes as its own column, remove _keep suffix, split out comma'd list of genes into individual columns up to last gene number which is 246, make this splitting out its own df and add metagene name as column so that can join dfs later on common colname
cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016 <- cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016 %>% 
  subset(!grepl("NMF metagene", 
                cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$...1)) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Metagene") 

cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene <- gsub("_keep",
                                                "", 
                                                cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene)

genesets_split <- str_split_fixed(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$...1, 
                                  ", ", 
                                  246) %>% 
  data.frame()

genesets_split$Metagene <- cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene

                                            genesets_split) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-`...1`) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Metagene") %>% 
  t() %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 201

# named vector of how many genes are in each metagene set
num_genes_meta <- colSums(!is.na(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016)) 

# check that all genes have been included and were appropriately transposed by checking gene numbers pre-transposing and after transposing (should be 11 TRUE); first extract NMF metagene rows from original df that had number of genes, then substring out the numbers as closely as possible and gsub out any extra characters and space, then check via table() if numbers are equivalent
test <- orig_metagene_gerrard_2016 %>% 
  subset(grepl("NMF metagene", 
               orig_metagene_gerrard_2016$...1)) %>% 
  as.vector()

test2 <- substring(test$...1, 
                   nchar(test$...1)-3) 

test_meta <- gsub(": ", 
                  "", 
                  test2) %>% 
  trimws()

table(num_genes_meta == test_meta,
      useNA = "always")

# to clean promoter states df, need to just split out gene from transcript ID joint column, so create a duplicate column for the gene and remove anything after : i.e. the transcript ID and any white space
cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020 <- orig_promoter_states_gerrard_2020

cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020$Gene <- cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020$`GENE:Transcript_id`

cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020 <- cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020 %>%
  relocate(Gene,
           .after = `GENE:Transcript_id`)

cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020$Gene <- gsub(x = cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020$Gene,
                                                  pattern = ":.*",
                                                  replacement = "") %>%
  trimws()

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020$Gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 1975

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020$Gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 705


# to clean lgpca df, need to make colnames more R friendly, remove PC listings before each tissue type
cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 <- orig_lgpca_gerrard_2016 %>%
  clean_names()

cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016$go_term <- gsub(".*: ",
                                           "",
                                           cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016$go_term)

# remove rows in limb section which have palate development, cranial skeleton, face morphogenesis gene sets
cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 <- cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016[-c(10, 14, 17),]

# make new column of tissues, remove any GO terms and carry down all tissues til next blank, rename limb development and add geneset description to tissue in new column, remove any rows without genes i.e. residual tissue placeholder rows, make tissue_GO rownames, move extreme genes to end of df
cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 <- cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 %>%
  transform(Tissue = go_term)

cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016$Tissue <- gsub("GO:.*",
                                          NA,
                                          cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016$Tissue)

cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 <- cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 %>%
  fill(Tissue) %>%
  transform(Tissue = ifelse(Tissue %in% c("Limb and palate development"),
                            "Limb development",
                            Tissue)) %>%
  transform(Tissue_GO = paste0(Tissue,
                               "_",
                               gene_ontology_description_biological_process_molecular_function_or_core_component)) %>%
  drop_na(extreme_genes) %>%
  relocate(extreme_genes,
           .after = Tissue)

# split out comma'd lists of lgpca genes into individual columns up to last gene number which is 478, make this splitting out its own df and add tissue_GO as column so that can join dfs later on common colname
lgpca_split <- str_split_fixed(cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016$extreme_genes,
                               ",",
                               478) %>%
  data.frame()

lgpca_split$Tissue_GO <- cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016$Tissue_GO


# join split genes to lgpca df, remove unneeded columns, replace blanks with NAs
cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 <- left_join(cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016,
                                        lgpca_split,
                                        by = "Tissue_GO") %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(1:6)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Tissue_GO") %>%
  t() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  remove_rownames()

cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016[cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 == ""] <- NA

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_lgpca_gerrard_2016 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# for DEGs of single-cell on 4-6wk embryos, creating a new column of developmental system tied to cluster annotation, removing now-irrelevant columns, making this new column the rows so that they become columns when transposed, making colnames R-friendly, and fixing misformatted gene names from original excel file
cleaned_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023 <- orig_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023 %>% 
  transform(System_annotation = paste0(Developmental_system,
                                       "_",
                                       Final_annotation)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(1:2)) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("System_annotation") %>% 
  t() %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  remove_rownames()


cleaned_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023[cleaned_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023 == "44622"] <- "MARCHF2"
cleaned_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023[cleaned_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023 == "44621"] <- "MARCHF1"


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_4to6wk_xu_2023 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_2148_fang_2010$symbol %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 13

# for temporal genes of whole embryo from Yi 2010, removing rows with no transcript ID, removing extraneous characters and any genes with hypothetical or similar listings, making colnames R-friendly, and fixing misformatted gene names from original excel file
cleaned_SOM_yi_2010 <- orig_SOM_yi_2010 %>% 
  drop_na(`Transcript ID`) %>%  
  mutate_at(.vars = colnames(orig_SOM_yi_2010),
            .funs = ~ str_replace(.,
                                  " ///.*",
                                  "")) %>%
  # subset(!grepl("hypothetical",
  #               `Gene Title`,
  #               ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  # subset(!grepl("similar to",
  #               `Gene Title`,
  #               ignore.case = TRUE)) %>% 
  clean_names()


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_SOM_yi_2010$gene_symbol %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_SOM_yi_2010$gene_symbol %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 118

# for gastrula markers, remove irrelevant column and rename columns to be more specific
cleaned_gastrula_markers_tyser_2021 <- orig_gastrula_markers_tyser_2021 %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Rank) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Epiblast = Epi,
                Ectoderm_amniotic_embryonic = EAE,
                Primitive_streak = PS,
                Nascent_mesoderm = NM,
                Emergent_mesoderm = EM,
                Advanced_mesoderm = AM,
                Extraembryonic_mesoderm = ExM,
                Axial_mesoderm = AXM,
                Endoderm = Endo,
                Haemato_endothelial_progenitors = HEP,
                Erythroblasts = Ery)


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_gastrula_markers_tyser_2021 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_gastrula_markers_tyser_2021 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 418

# for ATACdb sample metadata, making new sample column to facilitate joining with footprint data later on, making colnames more R-friendly, and collapsing down similar tissues into 1
cleaned_ATACdb_sample_metadata <- orig_ATACdb_sample_metadata %>% 
  transform(sample = `Sample ID`) %>% 
  relocate(sample,
           .after = 1) %>%  
  clean_names() %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(tissue_type %in% c("Peripheral blood",
                                                    "Myeloid",
                                                    "Hematopoietic"),
                                 "Blood",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(tissue_type %in% c("keratinocyte"),
                                 "Skin",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  # transform(tissue_type = ifelse(tissue_type %in% c("Forebrain"),
  #                                "Brain",
  #                                tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(tissue_type %in% c("Catilage"),
                                 "Cartilage",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(tissue_type %in% c("Ovarian",
                                                    "Ovarian cancer"),
                                 "Ovary",
                                 tissue_type))  %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(tissue_type %in% c("Mammary Gland"),
                                 "Breast",
                                 tissue_type))  %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("neutrophil",
                                                       "DP3 minus sorted B cell",
                                                       "B cell",
                                                       "GM12878"),
                                 "Blood",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("CRL7250"),
                                 "Fibroblast",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("RUES2"),
                                 "Embryo",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("Endometrial stromal cell"),
                                 "Uterus",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("Prostate"),
                                 "Prostate",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("Lung"),
                                 "Lung",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("Catilage"),
                                 "Cartilage",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(cancer_type %in% c("Glioblastoma"),
                                 "Brain",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(cancer_type %in% c("Ovarion cancer"),
                                 "Ovary",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("HAP1"),
                                 "Blood",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("Ishikawa"),
                                 "Uterus",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("TOV-21G"),
                                 "Ovary",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("WM989"),
                                 "Skin",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(tissue_type = ifelse(biosample_name %in% c("D283"),
                                 "Brain",
                                 tissue_type)) %>% 
  transform(cancer_type = ifelse(cancer_type %in% c("Ovarion cancer"),
                                 "Ovarian cancer",
                                 cancer_type)) %>% 
  transform(cancer_type = ifelse(cancer_type %in% c("Fibroscarcoma"),
                                 "Fibrosarcoma",
                                 cancer_type))

# for ATACdb footprints, making colnames R-friendly, new column to expressly say p53, and new sample column to match metadata for joining later on i.e. make numbers out to 4 digits with leading 0s as needed
cleaned_ATACdb_TF_footprint <- orig_ATACdb_TF_footprint %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  transform(TF = "TP53") %>% 
  transform(sample = sprintf("Sample_%04d", 
                             sample_id)) %>% 
  relocate(c(TF,
             sample),
           .after = tf_name)

  clean_names()

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_census_fischer_2017$gene_symbol %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_p73targets_rosenbluth_2011 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 20


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_p73targets_humancancer_153_wang_2020 %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# update gene names per fix_fixed table and genecards.org
cleaned_p73targets_humancancer_153_wang_2020[cleaned_p73targets_humancancer_153_wang_2020 == "VEGF-A"] <- "VEGFA"

# get pathways of interest from msigdbr

                            cleaned_human_all_msigdbr_GOBP$gs_name[grepl("^GOBP_EMBRYO.*", 
                                                                         cleaned_human_all_msigdbr_GOBP$gs_name)] %>%
                              unique(),
                            "GOBP_IN_UTERO_EMBRYONIC_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_REGULATION_OF_EMBRYONIC_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_ASTROCYTE_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_BRAIN_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_BONE_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_BONE_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_DIGESTIVE_SYSTEM_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_DIGESTIVE_TRACT_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_GLIAL_CELL_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_IMMUNE_SYSTEM_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_INTESTINAL_EPITHELIAL_CELL_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_KIDNEY_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_KIDNEY_EPITHELIUM_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_KIDNEY_MESENCHYME_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_LUNG_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_LUNG_EPITHELIUM_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_LIVER_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_MUSCLE_TISSUE_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_MUSCLE_ORGAN_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_MUSCLE_ORGAN_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_PANCREAS_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_PROSTATE_GLAND_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_PROSTATE_GLAND_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_SKIN_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_SKIN_EPIDERMIS_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_SKIN_MORPHOGENESIS",
                            "GOBP_STOMACH_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_THYROID_GLAND_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_UTERUS_DEVELOPMENT",
                            "GOBP_UTERUS_MORPHOGENESIS") %>% 
  trimws() %>% 
  na.omit() %>%
```
