```{r datacleaning, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = 'hide'}
  sort()

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_human_all_msigdbr_GOBP %>% 
  subset(gs_name %in% devel_msigdbr_pathways) %>% 
  pull(gene_symbol) %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_adrenal_DEGs_delvalle_2017$SYMBOL %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 23

# for delvalle 2023 adrenal DEGs, only keep genes with padj < 0.05 and logFC >= 1
cleaned_adrenal_DEGS_bulk_delvalle_2023 <- orig_adrenal_DEGS_bulk_delvalle_2023 %>% 
  subset(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange >= 1) %>% 
  distinct()


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_adrenal_DEGS_bulk_delvalle_2023$symbol %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# for del valle 2023 markers of clusters, only keep genes with logFC >= 0.25 and padj < 0.05 and pct1 >= 0.25 and at least 25% more present in pct1 vs pct2, arrange by cluster, decreasing logFC, log difference, decreasing pct1
cleaned_adrenal_markers_sc6w6d_delvalle_2023 <- orig_adrenal_markers_sc6w6d_delvalle_2023 %>% 
  subset(p_val_adj < 0.05 & avg_logFC >= 0.25 & pct.1 >= 0.25) %>% 
  transform(pct1_minus_pct2 = pct.1 - pct.2) %>% 
  subset(pct1_minus_pct2 >= 0.25) %>% 
  arrange(cluster, 
          -avg_logFC, 
          -pct1_minus_pct2, 
          -pct.1) %>% 
  distinct()

cleaned_adrenal_markers_sc6w_delvalle_2023 <- orig_adrenal_markers_sc6w_delvalle_2023 %>% 
  subset(p_val_adj < 0.05 & avg_logFC >= 0.25 & pct.1 >= 0.25) %>% 
  transform(pct1_minus_pct2 = pct.1 - pct.2) %>% 
  subset(pct1_minus_pct2 >= 0.25) %>% 
  arrange(cluster, 
          -avg_logFC, 
          -pct1_minus_pct2, 
          -pct.1) %>% 
  distinct()

cleaned_adrenal_markers_all_delvalle_2023 <- orig_adrenal_markers_all_delvalle_2023 %>% 
  subset(p_val_adj < 0.05 & avg_log2FC >= 0.25 & pct.1 >= 0.25) %>% 
  transform(pct1_minus_pct2 = pct.1 - pct.2) %>% 
  subset(pct1_minus_pct2 >= 0.25) %>% 
  arrange(-avg_log2FC,

          -pct.1) %>%

cleaned_adrenal_markers_sc6w6d_delvalle_2023[cleaned_adrenal_markers_sc6w6d_delvalle_2023 == "37681"] <- "MARCHF3"


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_adrenal_markers_sc6w6d_delvalle_2023$gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 9

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_20_zeng_2023$names %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)

  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%

  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%

           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_19_3wpc_zeng_2023$Gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 29

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_3to5wpc_zeng_2023$Gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023[cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023 == "2022-09-02"] <- "SEPTIN2"
cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023[cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023 == "2022-09-06"] <- "SEPTIN6"
cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023[cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023 == "2022-09-07"] <- "SEPTIN7"
cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023[cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023 == "2022-09-11"] <- "SEPTIN11"


# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_humanCNS_zeng_2023$Gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_lung_proerythro_cao_2023$names %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_PTNgenes_feng_2014$GeneSymbol %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be 114

# for limb and long bone development he 2021, keep genes with padj < 0.05 and logFC >= 0.25
cleaned_DEGs_limb_he_2021 <- orig_DEGs_limb_he_2021 %>% 
  subset(logfoldchanges >= 0.25 & pvals_adj < 0.05) %>% 
  distinct()

cleaned_DEGs_longbone_he_2021 <- orig_DEGs_longbone_he_2021 %>% 
  subset(logfoldchanges >= 0.25 & pvals_adj < 0.05) %>% 
  distinct()

cleaned_DEGs_calvaria_he_2021 <- orig_DEGs_calvaria_he_2021 %>% 
  subset(logfoldchanges >= 0.25 & pvals_adj < 0.05) %>% 
  distinct()

# use org.Hs.eg.db to identify which genes don't have ensembl i.e. are NA here and need to be updated (does have false negatives where genes do have ensembl IDs but they are not picked up, possibly because it is not latest ensembl on bioconductor?), run this every time to see if NAs change i.e. more gene names need to be updated
zed <- cleaned_DEGs_limb_he_2021$gene %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 1)

zed1 <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                              keys = zed$Genes, 
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>% 
  distinct(SYMBOL, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) 

table(is.na(zed1)) # NA should be

# check hgnc for newest gene names of older names which now don't have ensembl
fix <- hgnc::filter_by_keyword(tbl = hgnc_full, 
                               keyword = zed1 %>%
                                 subset(is.na(ENSEMBL)) %>%
                                 pull(SYMBOL) %>%
                                 paste0("^",
                                        .,
                                        "$"), # to get exact gene name matches
                               cols = c("prev_symbol", 
                                        "alias_symbol")) %>% # check old symbols columns
  dplyr::select(c(symbol, 
                  prev_symbol, 
                  alias_symbol))

# need to unnest list columns which have multiple old names for same new gene name; doing it sequentially like this makes it a cartesian product of rows although can't do all cols at once because uneven list lengths in cols
fix <- fix %>%
  unnest_longer(prev_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE)
fix <- fix %>% 
  unnest_longer(alias_symbol,
                keep_empty = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

cleaned_pancreas_enhancer_enriched_cebola_2015 <- orig_pancreas_enhancer_enriched_cebola_2015 %>% 
  subset(PValue < 0.05 & grepl("pancreas", 
                               `Term**`)) %>% 
  pull(Genes) %>% 
  str_split(.,
            ", ") %>% 
  unlist() %>% 
  unname() %>% 
  trimws() %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  sort()

  pull(`...7`) %>% 
  str_split(.,
            ", ") %>% 
  unlist() %>% 
  unname() %>% 
  trimws() %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  sort()

# melt down prev and alias symbols into 1 final column of old names so that just old and new cols left, only keep old names that are in dataset, remove NA old colnames meaning they already have old names accounted for, remove prev/alias symbol name column to allow them to collapse down, arrange alphabetically and rearrange cols to read old to new, and only keep distinct old names with first match of new name (because prev names melt first so they are prioritized when duplicates are dropped)
fix_fixed <- fix %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "symbol") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(prev_alias_symbol = value) %>%
  subset(prev_alias_symbol %in% zed1$SYMBOL) %>%
  drop_na(prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(variable)) %>%
  arrange(prev_alias_symbol) %>% 
  relocate(symbol,
           .after = prev_alias_symbol) %>%
  distinct(prev_alias_symbol,
           .keep_all = TRUE)

# for boettcher isogenic AML lines, already reduce to padj < 0.05 and abs(log2FC) >= 1 to get DEGs, left join with hgnc based on entrez id since some ensembl are missing to update gene names
cleaned_K562_DMSO_M237I_WT_boettcher_2019 <- orig_K562_DMSO_M237I_WT_boettcher_2019 %>% 
  subset(padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >= 1) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(orig_gene = Symbol) %>% 
  left_join(., 
            hgnc %>% 
              dplyr::select(c(symbol,
                              ensembl_gene_id,
                              entrez_id)),
            by = c("GeneID" = "entrez_id")) %>% 
  transform(symbol_to_use = symbol) %>% # retain old gene names without match so that present in venns
  transform(symbol_to_use = ifelse(is.na(symbol_to_use),
                                   orig_gene,
                                   symbol_to_use)) %>% 
  distinct()
```

$~$

# **Extracting Genes of Interest** {#getGOIs}

$~$

Now that there are multiple collections of genes deemed important for organogenesis and gastrulation, I will combine genes from metagenes, LgPCA, and gene sets in the @gerrard2016 and @gerrard2020 studies. I will look at genes in tissues which feature cancers often in patients with Li-Fraumeni syndrome (adrenal, brain, and upper/lower limb as a surrogate for bones and soft tissues) as well as tissues which feature cancers often in patients with somatic p53 mutations (lung, liver, kidney, and pancreas). These tissues were chosen as they are present in both @gerrard2016 and @gerrard2020 studies.

$~$

By visual inspection of panel A of Figure 1---figure supplement 5 in @gerrard2016, I have defined NMF metagenes as below and thus will use these metagenes for these tissues in subsequent code:

-   NMF metagene 1: thyroid
-   NMF metagene 2: liver
-   NMF metagene 3: kidney and testis
-   NMF metagene 4: RPE (retinal pigment epithelium)
-   NMF metagene 5: brain
-   NMF metagene 6: limbs and palate
-   NMF metagene 7: heart
-   NMF metagene 8: liver
-   NMF metagene 9: stomach, lung, tongue
-   NMF metagene 10: adrenal
-   NMF metagene 11: palate, pancreas, RPE

Consequently, I won't use metagenes to get genes for the kidney, limbs, lung, and pancreas as the genes are not discriminatory and other tissues are intermixed, and I will combine the unique genes from metagenes 2 and 8 for the liver. Moreover, I will combined the unique genes from the upper and lower limbs genesets.

$~$

For LgPCA genes, I will combine all unique genes listed for each tissue of interest, although there are no genesets for lung or pancreas.

$~$

Additionally, I am pulling out genes from the DEGs of 4-6wk embryos, temporally changing genes in the whole embryo, and markers in the CS7 gastrula.

$~$

```{r metagene-prep}
# get metagenes of each tissue of interest possible, remove NAs, only keep unique genes, sort alphabetically
adrenal_metagene <- cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene_10 %>% 
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>% 
  sort()

brain_metagene <- cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene_5 %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  sort()

liver_metagene <- c(cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene_2, 
                    cleaned_metagenes_gerrard_2016$Metagene_8) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  sort()
```

```{r promoter-states-prep, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = 'hide'}
# not using this to query database, but checking all known 230 p53 targets' promoter states in embryo to see if different epigenomic landscapes are why developmental target gene differences present in tissues
promoter_states_p53_prep <- cleaned_promoter_states_gerrard_2020 %>% 
  subset(Gene %in% census_cistrome_overlap) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-contains(c("cluster", 
                            "CpG", 
                            "line", 
                            "ranscript", 
                            "fetal", 
                            "adult", 
                            "palate",
                            "RPE", 
                            "ventricle"))) %>% # remove unnecessary columns
  arrange(Gene) %>% 
  distinct()

# convert promoter states to numerical scores so that can see general promoter expression across tissues
# inactive = 0, repressed = -1, broad = 1, narrow = 0.5, bidirectional = 0.25, expressed = 0.75
# consult figure 2a and 2b of gerrard 2020 paper as well to get sense of scoring
promoter_states_p53_prep_scored <- promoter_states_p53_prep %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:ncol(.)),
            ~ dplyr::case_when(. %in% c("INACTIVE") ~ "0",
                               . %in% c("REPRESSED") ~ "-1",
                               . %in% c("BROAD") ~ "1",
                               . %in% c("NARROW") ~ "0.5",
                               . %in% c("BI-DIR") ~ "0.25",
                               . %in% c("EXPRESSED") ~ "0.75",
                               TRUE ~ .)) %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:ncol(.)),
            as.numeric) %>% 
  distinct() 

# remove genes not differentially open across tissues i.e. consistently inactive or repressed, etc.
promoter_states_p53_prep_scored_filtered <- promoter_states_p53_prep_scored %>%
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 0 scores i.e. inactive in all tissues
            any_vars(. != 0)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only -1 scores i.e. repressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != -1)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 1 scores i.e. broad expressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != 1)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 0.5 scores i.e. narrow expressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != 0.5)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 0.25 scores i.e. bidirec expressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != 0.25)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 0.75 scores i.e. expressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != 0.75)) %>% 
  distinct()


# same as above, just defining all variations of expressed as 1 to be simpler, but lose nuances of genes so can only compare broader expression vs inactive or repressed differences

# convert promoter states to numerical scores so that can see general promoter expression across tissues
# inactive = 0, repressed = -1, broad = 1, narrow = 1, bidirectional = 1, expressed = 1
# consult figure 2a and 2b of gerrard 2020 paper as well to get sense of scoring
promoter_states_simple_p53_prep_scored <- promoter_states_p53_prep %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:ncol(.)),
            ~ dplyr::case_when(. %in% c("INACTIVE") ~ "0",
                               . %in% c("REPRESSED") ~ "-1",
                               . %in% c("BROAD") ~ "1",
                               . %in% c("NARROW") ~ "1",
                               . %in% c("BI-DIR") ~ "1",
                               . %in% c("EXPRESSED") ~ "1",
                               TRUE ~ .)) %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(2:ncol(.)),
            as.numeric) %>% 
  distinct() 

# remove genes not differentially open across tissues i.e. consistently inactive or repressed, etc.
promoter_states_simple_p53_prep_scored_filtered <- promoter_states_simple_p53_prep_scored %>%
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 0 scores i.e. inactive in all tissues
            any_vars(. != 0)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only -1 scores i.e. repressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != -1)) %>% 
  filter_at(vars(2:ncol(.)), # remove rows with only 1 scores i.e. some type of expressed in all tissues 
            any_vars(. != 1)) %>% 
  distinct()
```

# **Combining Genes of Interest For TargetGeneRegulation Database** {#combineGOIs}

$~$

Now that I have genes from each dataset, I am combining them into comma-separated vectors per dataset which is the format needed for the TargetGeneRegulation Database (next section) to assess putative p53 associations with them.

$~$

```{r combinedgenes, warning = FALSE}
# although create each geneset as csv row in excel file to save, to actually search targetgenereg, output 1 mega csv row that has all unique genes of all datasets so that minimal files are created and read back into R
what_to_query_targetgeneregdb <- list(mget(gsub("_csv$",
                                                "",
                                                ls(pattern = "_csv$")))) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort()

# get ensembl of all genes to query which will actually be searched in database

  subset(symbol %in% what_to_query_targetgeneregdb) %>% 
  pull(ensembl_gene_id) %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique() %>%
  sort()

                                                                                                        subset(symbol %in% what_to_query_targetgeneregdb) %>%
                                                                                                        pull(symbol)))]

                              keys = what_to_query_no_ensembl_match,  
                              keytype = "SYMBOL",
                              column = "ENSEMBL") %>%  
  distinct(SYMBOL,   
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  drop_na(ENSEMBL)
```

# **Read in Data From TargetGeneRegulation Database** {#readtargetgenesdata}

$~$

Now that I have lists of genes for each dataset, I inputted these genes into the TargetGeneRegulation Database [@fischer2022] (available at <http://www.targetgenereg.org/>) to see if these genes changed in expression after p53 perturbations in dozens of expression and ChIP-seq datasets. It also provides information on if p53 binds to the TSS or enhancers of genes. Due to the large number of genes which would otherwise crash the database if all were queried at once, I queried in 3 chunks - first alphabetical A-H genes, then I-R genes, then S-end of gene list. I then downloaded these results for each tissue and am reading them in below.

# **Identify Putative Developmental Genes Regulated by p53** {#findp53reggenes}

$~$

Now that I have information on genes from each dataset and their putative associations with p53, I can extract genes which have the most important putative associations. I am defining putative p53-regulated genes as genes with an absolute value of 5 or more for the p53 Expression Score (i.e. upregulated or downregulated after p53 perturbation in at least a net of 5 of 57 expression datasets) and subsetting to only genes which have either a p53 bound TSS or enhancer.

$~$

```{r findreggenes, warning = FALSE}

  subset(abs(as.numeric(p53_expression_score_55_to_57)) >= 5) %>% 
  subset(p53_bound_tss == "yes" | p53_bound_enhancer == "yes") %>% 
  arrange(desc(as.numeric(p53_expression_score_55_to_57)),
          desc(as.numeric(p53_median_log2fc))) %>%
  drop_na(symbol)

# combine family member and murine target gene overlap into df to output as table later
venn_family_df <- data.frame(lapply(mget(ls(pattern = "^reg_.*_overlap.*_genes$")) %>% head(-2),
                                        "length<-",
                                        max(lengths(mget(ls(pattern = "^reg_.*_overlap.*_genes$")) %>% head(-2))))) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  replace(is.na(.),
          "") %>%
  rownames_to_column("Overlap") %>% 
  transform(Overlap = gsub("_", 
                             " ", 
                             Overlap)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 2)
```

```{r p53reg-genes-grid, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.height = 26, fig.width = 20}
                  ifelse(`V1` %in% reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes,

  # rule_text_bold(`V1`,

  # rule_text_bold(`V2`,

  rule_text_color(`V3`,

  # rule_text_bold(`V3`,

  rule_text_color(`V4`,
                  ifelse(`V4` %in% reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes,

  # rule_text_bold(`V4`,
  #                expression = `V4` %in% reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes) %>% # stops italics
  rule_text_color(`V5`,
                  ifelse(`V5` %in% reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes,
                         "red",

  # rule_text_bold(`V5`,
```

# **Manual DEG Analyses of LFS, Isogenic p53 WT/mutant, and TCGA splicing-mutant/other-mutant Datasets**

$~$

$~$

```{r deseq, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = 'hide'}
# for tcga deseq, need to first create case-control pairs between splicing/other mutant

# first prepare data to be analysed in ccoptimalmatch algorithm based on vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ccoptimalmatch/vignettes/ccoptimalmatching_vignette.html>

# although 19 and 226 cases chosen from GDC, they were not based on matching sexes, so actual viable samples for DESeq will be much fewer once demographics and other parameters are matched

# make one df with both cases and controls in it to work on henceforth
tcga_case_ctrl_not_processed <- full_join(cleaned_tcga_other_mut_clinical,
                                          cleaned_tcga_splicing_mut_clinical)

# check if correct number of cases and controls
table(tcga_case_ctrl_not_processed$case_control, 
      useNA = "always") # should be 19 case 226 control

# step 1: exact matching on variables for data subsets
# to define subsets (factorial combination of variables), filter by cases, take distinct combination of variables, create new variable subset, select only relevant variables
create_tcga_subset <- tcga_case_ctrl_not_processed %>% 
  filter(case_control == "case") %>%
  arrange(project_id,
          #age_at_index,
          #ethnicity,
          gender,
          race,
          ajcc_pathologic_stage,
          #ajcc_pathologic_t,
          #icd_10_code, 
          primary_diagnosis,
          #tissue_or_organ_of_origin
          ) %>% # variables we want to match controls on
  distinct(project_id,
          #age_at_index,
          #ethnicity,
          gender,
          race,
          ajcc_pathologic_stage,
          #ajcc_pathologic_t,
          #icd_10_code, 
          primary_diagnosis,
          #tissue_or_organ_of_origin,
          .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(subset = 1:n()) %>%
  dplyr::select(project_id,
                #age_at_index,
                #ethnicity,
                gender,
                race,
                ajcc_pathologic_stage,
                #ajcc_pathologic_t,
                #icd_10_code, 
                primary_diagnosis,
                #tissue_or_organ_of_origin, 
                subset)

# merge data with subset variable with cases only and controls only
tcga_case_with_subset <- tcga_case_ctrl_not_processed %>% 
  filter(case_control == "case") %>%
  full_join(create_tcga_subset, 
            by = c('project_id',
          #'age_at_index',
          #'ethnicity',
          'gender',
          'race',
          'ajcc_pathologic_stage',
          #'ajcc_pathologic_t',
          #'icd_10_code', 
          'primary_diagnosis'
          #,'tissue_or_organ_of_origin'
          ))

tcga_control_with_subset <- tcga_case_ctrl_not_processed %>% 
  filter(case_control == "control") %>% # only retain controls matched to a subset
  inner_join(create_tcga_subset, 
             by = c('project_id',
          #'age_at_index',
          #'ethnicity',
          'gender',
          'race',
          'ajcc_pathologic_stage',
          #'ajcc_pathologic_t',
          #'icd_10_code', 
          'primary_diagnosis'
          #,'tissue_or_organ_of_origin'
          ))

# check which subsets are viable i.e. have at least 2 case samples for now; only these ones can be used at most for DESeq after controls are matched with the algorithm
table(tcga_case_with_subset$subset, 
      useNA = "always")

# see how many controls identified per subset for now
table(tcga_control_with_subset$subset, 
      useNA = "always")

# bind cases and ctrls which now have subset variable and check how many cases and ctrls left
not_processed <- rbind(tcga_case_with_subset,
                       tcga_control_with_subset)

table(not_processed$case_control, 
      useNA = "always")

# step 2: artificial observations and range of variables
# split into cases and controls and create variable cluster_case to depict cases separately, has levels based on total number of cases; empty in controls but have names of cases
bdd_controls <- not_processed[not_processed$case_control == "control", ]
bdd_controls$cluster_case <- 0
bdd_cases <- not_processed[not_processed$case_control == "case", ]
bdd_cases$cluster_case <- paste("case",
                                1:nrow(bdd_cases),
                                sep = "_")

# bind cases and ctrls which now have cluster_case variable and create age var
not_processed <- rbind(bdd_cases,
                       bdd_controls)

not_processed$age <- not_processed$age_at_index 

# again split cases and controls into diff datasets
bdd_cases <- not_processed[not_processed$case_control == "case",]
bdd_control <- not_processed[not_processed$case_control == "control",]

# make empty df and unique list of cluster_case
bdd_temp <- data.frame()
list_p <- unique(bdd_cases$cluster_case)

# loop to make pseudo-observations for controls; first identify in which subset each case belongs, then check which controls are in same subset and bind those controls to case, and select range for age, here absolute difference of age b/t case and control smaller than 5 is  chosen; since cases different in subsets in terms of age, each case will have diff number of controls available to pool

for(i in 1:length(list_p)){
 temp <- bdd_cases[bdd_cases$cluster_case == list_p[i], ]
 subset_identified <- temp$subset
 temp0 <- bdd_control[bdd_control$subset == temp$subset, ]
 temp_final <- rbind(temp, 
                     temp0)
 temp_final$cluster_case <- list_p[i]
 temp_final = temp_final %>%
            group_by(cluster_case) %>%
            mutate(age_diff = abs(age - age[case_control == "case"]))
 temp_final$age_fup <- ifelse(temp_final$age_diff <= 10,
                              "accept",
                              "delete")
 temp_final <- temp_final[temp_final$age_fup == "accept", ]
 temp_final$age_fup <- NULL
 bdd_temp <- rbind(bdd_temp,
                   temp_final)
}

# check case-control totals
table(bdd_temp$case_control, 
      useNA = "always")

# step 3: create total ctrls per case and freq of ctrls vars
# total controls per case depicts total pool of controls available for each case, case_ind takes value 1 if patient is case and 0 if control, select only relevant variables
bdd_temp = bdd_temp %>% 
  group_by(cluster_case) %>% 
  mutate(total_control_per_case = n() - 1)

bdd_temp$case_ind <- ifelse(bdd_temp$case_control == "case",
                            1,
                            0)

bdd_temp <- subset(bdd_temp, 
                   select = c(cluster_case, 
                              case_control, 
                              case_ind,
                              age_diff, 
                              total_control_per_case,
                              subset,
                              case_submitter_id, # patient ID
                              project_id,
                              age_at_index,
                              ethnicity,
                              gender,
                              race,
                              ajcc_pathologic_stage,
                              ajcc_pathologic_t,
                              icd_10_code, 
                              primary_diagnosis,
                              tissue_or_organ_of_origin
                   ))


# freq of ctrls is how many times control assigned to case
bdd_temp = bdd_temp %>% 
  group_by(case_submitter_id) %>% 
  mutate(freq_of_controls = n()) %>% 
  ungroup()

# see how many times ctrls are assigned, as ctrls with lowest frequency matched first leaving high freq ctrls for other cases and that age diffs and freq of ctrls still needs to be optimized in next step
head(bdd_temp, 10)

# step 4: order variables
# critical to order vars by most to least important parameters
bdd_temp <- bdd_temp[order(bdd_temp$subset,
                         bdd_temp$case_control,
                         bdd_temp$project_id,
                         bdd_temp$gender,
                         bdd_temp$race,
                         bdd_temp$primary_diagnosis,
                         bdd_temp$ajcc_pathologic_stage,
                         bdd_temp$age_diff,
                         bdd_temp$freq_of_controls,
                         bdd_temp$cluster_case), ]

# check cases to see closest ctrls ordered after cases with optimal age diff and that freq of ctrls ordered such that ctrls with lowest freq matched first
head(bdd_temp, 10)

# now data ready for algorithm
# how the algorithm works:
# 1. Start of round 1. Select one control per case per iteration. Select first control which is closest, thus most optimal.
# 2. Split between duplicated and unique controls, and assign duplicated controls to case that has less available controls to pool.
# 3. Exclude cases that already have at least 1 control. Also exclude controls matched to a case.
# 4. Repeat steps 1-3 until all cases have at least 1 control (where applicable).
# 5. End of round 1. Continue to round 2 up to round n, where n is controls to match. If 4 controls needed, then 4 rounds, if 10 controls are needed then 10 rounds.
final_data <- optimal_matching(bdd_temp, 
                               n_con = 10, #  num controls wanted per case
                               cluster_case, 
                               case_submitter_id, # patient ID
                               total_control_per_case, 
                               case_control, 
                               with_replacement = FALSE)


# see first 20 rows
final_data <- final_data %>% 
  arrange(cluster_case)

head(final_data, 20)

# to see how many ctrls matched for each case
final_data = final_data %>% 
  group_by(cluster_case) %>% 
  mutate(total_control_matched = n() - 1) %>% 
  ungroup()

table(final_data$case_control,
      final_data$total_control_matched, 
      useNA = "always")

# number of cases and controls per subset, can only use subsets with at least 2 cases and ctrls
table(final_data$case_control,
      final_data$subset, 
      useNA = "always")

# pull out viable contrasts, i.e. at least 2 cases and ctrls present
tcga_cases_ctrls_final <- final_data %>% 
  subset(subset %in% (final_data %>% 
                        subset(case_control == "case") %>% 
                        group_by(subset) %>%
                        dplyr::count() %>%
                        filter(n >= 2) %>%
                        pull(subset))) %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(case_control,
                  age_diff,
                  subset,
                  case_submitter_id,
                  project_id,
                  age_at_index,
                  ethnicity,
                  gender,
                  race,
                  ajcc_pathologic_stage,
                  ajcc_pathologic_t,
                  icd_10_code, 
                  primary_diagnosis,
                  tissue_or_organ_of_origin))


# pull out filenames that correspond to chosen cases; can rbind because same columns
tcga_manifest_final <- rbind((cleaned_tcga_other_mut_manifest %>% 
                               subset(case_id %in% tcga_cases_ctrls_final$case_submitter_id) %>% 
                               arrange(case_id) %>%

                             (cleaned_tcga_splicing_mut_manifest %>% 
                               subset(case_id %in% tcga_cases_ctrls_final$case_submitter_id) %>% 
                               arrange(case_id) %>%  
                               remove_rownames() %>% 
                               distinct())) %>% 
  distinct()

tcga_manifest_final <- left_join(tcga_manifest_final,
                                 (tcga_cases_ctrls_final %>% 
                                    subset(case_submitter_id %in% tcga_manifest_final$case_id) %>% 
                                    dplyr::select(c(case_submitter_id,
                                                    case_control,
                                                    subset))),
                                 by = c("case_id" = "case_submitter_id")) %>%

# put together all possible combinations of file paths to read in files
zed <- as.list(c((paste0(paste0(input_path,

       tcga_manifest_final$file_id,
       "/",
       tcga_manifest_final$file_name) %>% 
  gsub(pattern = "\\.gz$", # remove zipped file suffix
       "",
       .))))

# see whether file paths are valid, and subset list to only true file paths
zed <- zed[which((lapply(1:length(zed), 
               function(x) file.exists(zed[[x]]))) == "TRUE")]

# read in all files from filepaths, add temporary names to list elements e.g. folders for gene counts tables
zed_select <- zed[which(lapply(1:length(zed),

tcga_all_gene_counts_list <- lapply(1:length(zed_select),

names(tcga_all_gene_counts_list) <- str_extract(zed_select,

                                               names(i)[4:ncol(i)] <- paste0(names(tcga_all_gene_counts_list)[[x]],

# prefix cleaned up in mut prot col, rename col, encode NA as text, only keep mut prot, assoc cols, gene name in each df, hgnc joined based on ensembl, add list names to mut prot colnames 
tcga_all_muts_samples_named_list <- lapply(1:length(tcga_all_muts_list),
                                           FUN = function(x){
                                             i <- tcga_all_muts_list[[x]]
                                             i$HGVSp_Short <- gsub("^p.",
                                                                   "",
                                                                   i$HGVSp_Short)
                                             i <- i %>% 
                                               dplyr::rename(ProtChange = HGVSp_Short,
                                                             ensembl_gene_id = Gene) %>% # ensembl
                                               mutate(ProtChange = ifelse(is.na(ProtChange),
                                                                          "NA",
                                                                          as.character(ProtChange))) %>% 
                                               dplyr::select(c(ProtChange,
                                                               ensembl_gene_id,
                                                               Variant_Classification,
                                                               Variant_Type,
                                                               Consequence)) %>% 
                                               left_join(.,
                                                         hgnc %>% 
                                                           dplyr::select(c(symbol,
                                                                           ensembl_gene_id,
                                                                           entrez_id,
                                                                           locus_group,
                                                                           name)),
                                                         by = "ensembl_gene_id") %>%
                                               relocate(c(entrez_id,
                                                          locus_group,
                                                          name,
                                                          symbol,
                                                          ProtChange),
                                                        .after = ensembl_gene_id)
                                             names(i)[6:ncol(i)] <- paste0(names(tcga_all_muts_list)[[x]],
                                                                           "_",
                                                                           names(i)[6:ncol(i)])
                                             i
                                           })

                                FUN = function(x) tcga_all_muts_samples_named_list[[x]] %>%
                                  subset(symbol == "TP53") %>%
                                  dplyr::select(contains("ProtChange")) %>%
                                  pull(),
                                simplify = FALSE, # keep as list
                                USE.NAMES = TRUE) %>% 
  bind_rows() %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
  dplyr::rename(ProtChange = V1) %>%
  mutate(contrast = sample) %>%
  mutate(contrast = gsub(".*_c",
                         "",

  mutate(contrast = paste0("c",
                           contrast)) %>%
  arrange(contrast,
          parse_number(ProtChange))

                      mutate(temp = paste0(ProtChange,
                                           "_",
                                           contrast)) %>%
                      group_by(temp) %>%
                      summarize(n = n()) %>% 
                      subset(n > 1) %>% 
                      pull(temp) %>%
                      unique())) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(temp)) %>%
  mutate(temp = parse_number(contrast))

  dplyr::select(-c(temp,

  mutate(case = sample) %>%

# did results() on original integrated dds object but because K562 accounts for most of the variance in PCA it was not having any signif devel genes later on, so now doing results per individual dds object


res_K562_R175H_vs_WT <- results(dds_K562_R175H, 
                                contrast = c("Pairs",
                                             "K562 R175H",
                                             "K562 WT"), # control is second
                                alpha = 0.05, 
                                pAdjustMethod = "BH")
res_K562_R175H_vs_WT_shrink <- lfcShrink(dds_K562_R175H, 
                                  type = "ashr", # better shrinkage than normal and still allows contrasts
                                  res = res_K562_R175H_vs_WT) # for ashr don't need contrasts if res given

#summary(res_K562_R175H_vs_WT)

res_K562_R175H_vs_WT_signif <- res_K562_R175H_vs_WT_shrink %>% # use shrunken LFC for more accuracy
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >= 1) %>% 
  arrange(-log2FoldChange) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("row") %>% 
  left_join(.,
            hgnc %>% 
              dplyr::select(c(symbol,
                              ensembl_gene_id,
                              entrez_id)),
            by = c("row" = "ensembl_gene_id")) %>%
  dplyr::rename("ensembl_gene_id" = "row")

# make lists of all upreg, all downreg, in ensembl and gene names, for each contrast
DESeq_upreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list <- lapply(mget(ls(pattern = "^res_.*_vs_WT_shrink$")),
                                                FUN = function (x) x %>%
                                                  subset(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange >= 1) %>%
                                                  rownames() %>%
                                                  trimws() %>%
                                                  na.omit() %>%
                                                  unique())

DESeq_downreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list <- lapply(mget(ls(pattern = "^res_.*_vs_WT_shrink$")),
                                                  FUN = function (x) x %>%
                                                    subset(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange <= -1) %>%
                                                    rownames() %>%
                                                    trimws() %>%
                                                    na.omit() %>%
                                                    unique())

DESeq_upreg_per_contrast_genes_list <- lapply(1:length(DESeq_upreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list),
                                         FUN = function (x) DESeq_upreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list[[x]] %>% 
                                           data.frame() %>%
                                           dplyr::rename(ensembl_gene_id = 1) %>%
                                           left_join(.,
                                                     hgnc %>% 
                                                       dplyr::select(c(symbol,
                                                                       ensembl_gene_id,
                                                                       entrez_id)),
                                                     by = "ensembl_gene_id") %>%
                                           pull(symbol))
names(DESeq_upreg_per_contrast_genes_list) <- names(DESeq_upreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list)

DESeq_downreg_per_contrast_genes_list <- lapply(1:length(DESeq_downreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list),
                                         FUN = function (x) DESeq_downreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list[[x]] %>% 
                                           data.frame() %>%
                                           dplyr::rename(ensembl_gene_id = 1) %>%
                                           left_join(.,
                                                     hgnc %>% 
                                                       dplyr::select(c(symbol,
                                                                       ensembl_gene_id,
                                                                       entrez_id)),
                                                     by = "ensembl_gene_id") %>%
                                           pull(symbol))
names(DESeq_downreg_per_contrast_genes_list) <- names(DESeq_downreg_per_contrast_ensembl_list)
```

```{r deseq-pca-allsamples, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 7, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = 'hide'}
# make PCA
plotPCA(vst(dds), 
        intgroup = c("Cells",
                     "Condition")) + # whatever parameters you want from sample metadata
  labs(color = "Group") +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#000000",
                                "#E69F00",
                                "#56B4E9",
                                "#CC79A7",
                                "#009E73",
                                "purple",
                                "darkgray",
                                "red")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                 size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                  face = "bold",
                                  size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(5,0,0,0,"mm")),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(0,5,0,0,"mm")),
        legend.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                    face = "bold",
                                    size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                   size = 14),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5,
                                  color = "black",
                                  face = "bold",
                                  size = 16,
                                  margin = margin(0,0,5,0,"mm")),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# **Preparing Data For Clustered Heatmap of Putative p53-Regulated Genes and Tissues** {#heatmapprep}

$~$

To create a clustered heatmap of which putative p53-regulated developmental genes arise from which datasets (and consequently which tissues in development), I am creating a matrix of the presence of each putative p53-regulated developmental gene in each dataset with boolean TRUE/FALSE logic translated to 1 and 0, respectively.

```{r heatmap-prep}
# combine each dataset's genes into a list and rename to just tissues/germ layers
overlap_comparison_prep <- list(mget(ls(pattern = "_combined_genes$")))

overlap_comparison_list <- unlist(list(unlist(overlap_comparison_prep, 
                                              recursive = FALSE)),
                                  recursive = FALSE)

names(overlap_comparison_list) <- gsub("_combined.*",
                                       "",
                                       names(overlap_comparison_list))

# test whether regulated genes are in each dataset, reporting TRUE/FALSE, rename columns to dataset names and add column of genes
overlap_comparison <- lapply(names(overlap_comparison_list),
                             function(x) reg_targetgenes_db_genes %in% overlap_comparison_list[[x]]) %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  rename_all(~ names(overlap_comparison_list)) %>%
  add_column(Gene = reg_targetgenes_db_genes) %>%
  relocate(Gene,
           .before = 1)

overlap_triple_comparison <- lapply(names(overlap_comparison_list),
                                    function(x) reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes %in% overlap_comparison_list[[x]]) %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  rename_all(~ names(overlap_comparison_list)) %>% 
  add_column(Gene = reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes) %>% 
  relocate(Gene,
           .before = 1)

# to show number of p53-regulated genes out of number of total genes per dataset for complex heatmap row labels, need to get list before reshape::acast to say dataset (X reg out of Y total) (%)

# create list of which genes in each dataset were p53-reg
regs_per_dataset_list <- lapply(names(overlap_comparison_list),
                                function(x) (intersect(reg_targetgenes_db_genes,
                                                       overlap_comparison_list[[x]])) %>%
                                  na.omit() %>%
                                  unique() %>%
                                  sort())

names(regs_per_dataset_list) <- names(overlap_comparison_list)

regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_list <- lapply(names(overlap_comparison_list),
                                               function(x) (intersect(reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes,
                                                                      overlap_comparison_list[[x]])) %>% 
                                                 na.omit() %>% 
                                                 unique() %>% 
                                                 sort())

names(regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_list) <- names(overlap_comparison_list)

regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_df <- data.frame(lapply(regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_list,
                                                        "length<-",
                                                        max(lengths(regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_list)))) %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  replace(is.na(.),
          "") %>%
  rownames_to_column("Tissue") %>% 
  mutate(Tissue = gsub("_", 
                       " ",
                       Tissue)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Genes = 2)

# count how many p53-regulated genes were in each dataset

  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>%
  as.numeric()

# count how many total genes were in each dataset
genes_per_dataset_num_vector <- lapply(names(overlap_comparison_list), 
                                       FUN = function(x) overlap_comparison_list[[x]] %>%

  unlist() %>%
  unname() %>% 
  as.numeric()

# create vector of dataset (X reg out of Y total) (%)
dataset_reg_total_percent_char_vector <- lapply(c(1:length(colnames(overlap_comparison)[-1])),
                                                FUN = function(x) paste0(colnames(overlap_comparison)[-1][x],
                                                                         " (",
                                                                         regs_per_dataset_num_vector[x],
                                                                         " reg out of ",
                                                                         genes_per_dataset_num_vector[x],
                                                                         " total) (",
                                                                         format(regs_per_dataset_num_vector[x]/genes_per_dataset_num_vector[x] * 100,
                                                                                digits = 3),
                                                                         "%)")) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unname()

dataset_reg_triple_overlap_total_percent_char_vector <- lapply(c(1:length(colnames(overlap_triple_comparison)[-1])),

                                                                                        " (",
                                                                                        regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_num_vector[x],
                                                                                        " known out of ",
                                                                                        genes_per_dataset_num_vector[x],
                                                                                        " total) (",
                                                                                        format(regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_num_vector[x]/genes_per_dataset_num_vector[x] * 100,
                                                                                               digits = 3),
                                                                                        "%)")) %>%

                  value.var = 'Present')

# convert all lists of downreg devel genes of tissues in LFS and isogenic studies to df; first combine all lists into flattened list and rename elements to get down to tissue and dataset level, then make df of each dataset going vertically with genes
all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list <- unlist(mget(ls(pattern = "_DEGs_down_")[sapply(ls(pattern = "_DEGs_down_"),
                                                                                          function(i) class(get(i))) == "list"]),
                                                  recursive = FALSE)

names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) <- gsub("DEGs_down_.*\\.|_WT.*|_DMSO|_vs",
                                                       "",
                                                       names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list)) 
names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) <- gsub("regs_triple_overlap",
                                                       "known_hp53-reg",
                                                       names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list))  
names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) <- gsub("_",
                                                       " ",
                                                       names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list)) 
names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) <- gsub("astros LFS|astros",
                                                       "LFS astrocytes",
                                                       names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list))
names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) <- gsub("breastepi LFS",
                                                       "LFS breast epi",
                                                       names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list))
names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) <- gsub("osteoblasts LFS|osteo",
                                                       "LFS osteoblasts",
                                                       names(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list))

# ensure all vectors in list are sorted alphabetically
all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list <- lapply(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list, 
                                                  sort)

# convert to df
all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df <- data.frame(lapply(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list,
                                                           "length<-",
                                                           max(lengths(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list)))) %>%
  t() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  replace(is.na(.),
          "")

rownames(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df) <- gsub("\\.",
                                                        " ",
                                                        rownames(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df))

# get numbers of downreg genes in LFS and isogenic per tissue or germ layer and eventually put into matrix for heatmap as simpler way to see how many downreg genes across tissues than dozens of venn diagrams, which are still useful for double checking numbers and simpler visuals though
all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts <- lengths(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_list) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Dataset") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Downreg = 2) 

all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts[c("Tissue", 
                                               "Mutation")] <- str_split_fixed(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts$Dataset, 
                                                                                         " DEGs down | res ", 
                                                                                         2)

all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts <- left_join(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts,
                                                          lengths(regs_triple_overlap_per_dataset_list) %>% 
                                                            as.data.frame() %>% 
                                                            rownames_to_column("Tissue") %>% 
                                                            dplyr::rename(Genes = 2) %>%
                                                            mutate(Tissue = gsub("_",
                                                                                 " ",
                                                                                 Tissue)),
                                                          by = "Tissue") %>%
  mutate(Genes = ifelse(Tissue == "known hp53-reg",
                        length(reg_triple_overlap_targetgenes_db_genes),
                        Genes)) %>%
  mutate(Tissue = paste0(Tissue,
                         " (",
                         Genes,
                         " known p53 targets in development)"))

all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts <- all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts %>%
  drop_na(Genes)









all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts <- left_join(all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts,
          lengths(mget(ls(pattern = "^DEGs_down_.*_WT"))) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Mutation") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Total = 2) %>%
  mutate(Mutation = gsub("DEGs_down_|_WT.*",
                                          "",
                                          Mutation)) %>%
  mutate(Mutation = gsub("_DMSO_|_",
                         " ",
                         Mutation)) %>%
  mutate(Mutation = gsub("astros LFS",
                           "LFS astrocytes",
                           Mutation)) %>%
  mutate(Mutation = gsub("breastepi LFS",
                           "LFS breast epi",
                           Mutation)) %>%
  mutate(Mutation = gsub("osteoblasts LFS",
                           "LFS osteoblasts",
                           Mutation)),
          by = "Mutation") %>%
  mutate(Mutation = paste0(Mutation, 
                           " (",
                           Total,
                           " genes downregulated)"))

all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts_matrix <- all_tissues_DEGs_down_LFS_isogenic_df_counts %>%
  subset(!(str_detect(Dataset, 
                      "K562|breast"))) %>% # remove lines that don't match b/t GEO2R and deseq
  subset(str_detect(Dataset, 
                     "res")) %>% # keep deseq derived downreg devel gene numbers
  dplyr::select(c(Tissue,
                  Mutation,
                  Downreg)) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Tissue,
              names_from = Mutation,
              values_from = Downreg) %>%
  mutate(Tissue = gsub("known hp53-reg",
                          "all known targets",
                          Tissue)) %>%
  mutate(Tissue = gsub("adrenal",
                          "adrenal gland",
                          Tissue)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Tissue") %>%
  as.matrix()
```
